note: The main banks: CIBC Caribbean, RBC Royal Bank and Scotiabank, the three card issuers in the Turks and Caicos Financial Services Commission's schedule of domestic banks' rates and charges (as at June 2026). CIBC Caribbean's Turks and Caicos schedule of charges for cards (effective April 2020, last updated July 2026), read in full: its four personal Visa cards in US dollars, each with its annual fee for the primary card (none where it gives $0.00; the British Airways Visa Platinum's waived for its first year), its yearly purchase and cash advance rates, its 3% cash advance fee (at least $5 on the Visa Classic), its $50 late payment, $40 over limit and $40 returned cheque fees, and its late payment rate as the penalty rate. Its commercial cards aren't written, nor are the replacement, statement, rush card, emergency payment and auto-payment charges, which a holder meets only by asking or by an auto-payment. It states no minimum payment, grace period or foreign transaction fee. RBC Royal Bank's Turks and Caicos credit cards page (rendered 30 October 2026): its personal RBC Rewards Visa Platinum, Visa Gold and Visa Classic International, each with its annual fee and its 18% purchase and cash advance rates; the Commission's schedule adds RBC's Visa cash advance charge of 3% (at least $5), its $40 late payment fee and its $35 over limit fee. RBC's business and corporate cards aren't written. Scotiabank's Mastercard is in the Commission's schedule ($165 a year; a 2.5% to 3.0% cash advance charge; a $38.50 to $55.00 late fee) but no source read states its interest rate, so it isn't written. This file kept RBC's Visa Classic International, read on 29 October 2026, and adds the rest. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) looked for more banks and added none: Scotiabank Turks and Caicos's rates and fees pages give no credit card rate (its schedule of charges names only a premium account fee charged to a card), so its Mastercard still can't be written.
